newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC defies predictions, price surges.
newsitem.headline: HSBC defies predictions, price surges.

text.p: Banking giant HSBC Holdings Ltd recovered from a slide following its annual results announcement by surging for two consecutive days on Wednesday and Thursday.
Brokers had predicted the share price would be hit if the global banking group's results were not substantially better than forecast, analysts said.
HSBC Holdings reported growth in profit attributable to shareholders of 25 percent for 1996 on Monday, just slightly higher than a market consensus estimate of 24 percent.
The counter, which fell HK$2.50 on Tuesday, clawed back part of the loss on Wednesday by putting on HK$1.50 and gained HK$2.50 to HK$190.50 on Thursday.

Its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd, on the other hand, has fallen steadily since disappointing the market on Monday with an earnings growth of 6.3 percent compared with a consensus forecast of 16.0 percent.
It shed HK$4.25 on Tuesday, fell $1.25 on Wednesday and slipped HK$0.50 to close at HK$83.50 on Thursday, well off from its pre-results price of HK$89.50.
"The price of HSBC is now trading at 2.3 times the value of Hang Seng Bank, up from 1.4 times in April last year," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston.
"This shows how much HSBC has outperformed Hang Seng Bank and the market," Verin said. "This is the widest gap (between the two share prices) seen in the last 12 months."
HSBC's 1996 results report showed further improvement in its capital ratios, sparking renewed speculation that it would be seeking to make additional large acquisitions.
The international benchmark calls for tier one capital backing, chiefly shareholders'funds, equal to four percent of a bank's total risk-weighted assets and total capital ratio of eight percent.
HSBC's capital backing is nearly twice the prescribed level and Hang Seng Bank's about three times.

Senior bank executives have said that the reasons for the high capital ratios are the higher operating risks of some of the countries in which the bank operates and a lack of adequate deposit taking insurance in certain jursidictions.
